claim: The outer membrane (OM) of Gram-negative bacteria functions as a selective permeability barrier.
source: The outer membrane (OM) of Gram-negative bacteria functions as a selective permeability barrier.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in microbiology supported by citation (Nikaido, 2003) in the manuscript.

claim: Escherichia coli periplasmic Zn-metallopeptidase BepA contributes to the maintenance of OM integrity through its involvement in the biogenesis and degradation of LptD.
source: Escherichia coli periplasmic Zn-metallopeptidase BepA contributes to the maintenance of OM integrity through its involvement in the biogenesis and degradation of LptD, a β-barrel protein component of the lipopolysaccharide translocon.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the authors' previous work, supported by citations.

claim: BepA either promotes the maturation of LptD when it is on the normal assembly pathway (on-pathway) or degrades it when its assembly is compromised (off-pathway).
source: BepA either promotes the maturation of LptD when it is on the normal assembly pathway (on-pathway) or degrades it when its assembly is compromised (off-pathway).
evidence: This dual function is established from previous studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: BepA performs these functions probably on the β‐barrel assembly machinery (BAM) complex.
source: BepA performs these functions probably on the β‐barrel assembly machinery (BAM) complex.
evidence: This is stated as a probable mechanism based on previous research.

claim: The interaction of the BepA edge-strand located adjacent to the active site with LptD was crucial for proteolysis of LptD.
source: We found that the interaction of the BepA edge-strand located adjacent to the active site with LptD was crucial not only for proteolysis but also, unexpectedly, for assembly promotion of LptD.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated through mutational and crosslinking experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: The interaction of the BepA edge-strand with LptD was crucial for assembly promotion of LptD.
source: We found that the interaction of the BepA edge-strand located adjacent to the active site with LptD was crucial not only for proteolysis but also, unexpectedly, for assembly promotion of LptD.
evidence: This is an unexpected finding demonstrated through pulse-chase experiments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The unstructured N-terminal half of the β-barrel-forming domain of an immature LptD contacts with the BepA edge-strand.
source: Site-directed crosslinking analyses indicated that the unstructured N-terminal half of the β-barrel-forming domain of an immature LptD contacts with the BepA edge-strand.
evidence: This is demonstrated through photo-crosslinking and disulfide crosslinking experiments shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The C-terminal region of the β-barrel-forming domain of the BepA-bound LptD intermediate interacted with a 'seam' strand of BamA.
source: Furthermore, the C-terminal region of the β-barrel-forming domain of the BepA-bound LptD intermediate interacted with a 'seam' strand of BamA, suggesting that BepA recognized LptD assembling on the BAM complex.
evidence: This is demonstrated through crosslinking experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: BepA recognized LptD assembling on the BAM complex.
source: Furthermore, the C-terminal region of the β-barrel-forming domain of the BepA-bound LptD intermediate interacted with a 'seam' strand of BamA, suggesting that BepA recognized LptD assembling on the BAM complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the crosslinking data showing simultaneous interaction of LptD with both BepA and BamA.

claim: Irregularities in OMP biogenesis result in elevated cellular sensitivity to toxic compounds.
source: Therefore, irregularities in OMP biogenesis result in elevated cellular sensitivity to toxic compounds (Hart et al., 2019; Oh et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: After synthesis in the cytoplasm and following translocation across the IM to the periplasm through the SecYEG translocon, OMPs are delivered to the OM by periplasmic chaperones such as DegP, Skp, and SurA.
source: After synthesis in the cytoplasm and following translocation across the IM to the periplasm through the SecYEG translocon, OMPs are delivered to the OM by periplasmic chaperones such as DegP, Skp, and SurA, and are finally integrated into the OM (Konovalova et al., 2017; Plummer and Fleming, 2016; Ricci and Silhavy, 2019).
evidence: This describes the established pathway for OMP biogenesis, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The OM assembly of OMPs is mediated by the β-barrel assembly machinery (BAM) complex consisting of a β-barrel OMP, BamA, and four lipoproteins, namely BamB, BamC, BamD, and BamE.
source: The OM assembly of OMPs is mediated by the β-barrel assembly machinery (BAM) complex consisting of a β-barrel OMP, BamA, and four lipoproteins, namely BamB, BamC, BamD, and BamE (Plummer and Fleming, 2016; Ricci and Silhavy, 2019; Tomasek and Kahne, 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the BAM complex composition, supported by citations.

claim: BamA and BamD are the only essential components of the BAM complex.
source: Among the BAM complex subunits, BamA and BamD are the only essential components, although recent studies have shown that certain BamA mutations render all other BAM subunits dispensable (Hart et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hart et al., 2020.

claim: Certain BamA mutations render all other BAM subunits dispensable.
source: Among the BAM complex subunits, BamA and BamD are the only essential components, although recent studies have shown that certain BamA mutations render all other BAM subunits dispensable (Hart et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a recent finding cited from Hart et al., 2020.

claim: The BAM complex has a silk-hat-like structure.
source: The BAM complex has a silk-hat-like structure (Bakelar et al., 2016; Gu et al., 2016; Han et al., 2016; Iadanza et al., 2016; Tomasek et al., 2020); the OM-embedded C-terminal β-barrel domain of BamA forms the 'crown' and the N-terminal periplasmic polypeptide transport-associated (POTRA) domains of BamA form the 'brim' together with the BamB/C/D/E lipoproteins.
evidence: This structural description is supported by multiple structural studies cited.

claim: The OM-embedded C-terminal β-barrel domain of BamA forms the 'crown' of the silk-hat-like structure.
source: The BAM complex has a silk-hat-like structure (Bakelar et al., 2016; Gu et al., 2016; Han et al., 2016; Iadanza et al., 2016; Tomasek et al., 2020); the OM-embedded C-terminal β-barrel domain of BamA forms the 'crown' and the N-terminal periplasmic polypeptide transport-associated (POTRA) domains of BamA form the 'brim' together with the BamB/C/D/E lipoproteins.
evidence: This is a structural description supported by citations.

claim: The N-terminal periplasmic polypeptide transport-associated (POTRA) domains of BamA form the 'brim' together with the BamB/C/D/E lipoproteins.
source: The BAM complex has a silk-hat-like structure (Bakelar et al., 2016; Gu et al., 2016; Han et al., 2016; Iadanza et al., 2016; Tomasek et al., 2020); the OM-embedded C-terminal β-barrel domain of BamA forms the 'crown' and the N-terminal periplasmic polypeptide transport-associated (POTRA) domains of BamA form the 'brim' together with the BamB/C/D/E lipoproteins.
evidence: This is a structural description supported by citations.

claim: A heterodimer of LptD, a β-barrel OMP, and LptE, a lipoprotein, plays roles in the final step to insert LPS into the OM.
source: A heterodimer of LptD, a β-barrel OMP, and LptE, a lipoprotein, plays roles in the final step to insert LPS into the OM (Dong et al., 2014; Qiao et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about LPS transport, supported by citations.

claim: The mature form of LptD possesses two disulfide bonds formed by non-consecutive pairs of Cys residues (C31–C724 and C173–C725).
source: The mature form of LptD possesses two disulfide bonds formed by non-consecutive pairs of Cys residues (C31–C724 and C173–C725) (Ruiz et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a structural feature of mature LptD, supported by citation.

claim: An assembly intermediate of LptD having disulfide bonds formed by consecutive pairs of the Cys residues (C31–C173 and C724–C725) (LptDC) is first generated and isomerized to LptDNC during its assembly/maturation.
source: It has been shown, however, that an assembly intermediate of LptD having disulfide bonds formed by consecutive pairs of the Cys residues (C31–C173 and C724–C725) (LptDC; LptD with Consecutive disulfide bods) is first generated and isomerized to LptDNC (LptD with Non-Consecutive disulfide bonds) during its assembly/maturation, which is triggered by the association of LptD with LptE (Chng et al., 2012; Narita et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the LptD assembly pathway, supported by citations.

claim: The LptDC to LptDNC conversion is triggered by the association of LptD with LptE.
source: It has been shown, however, that an assembly intermediate of LptD having disulfide bonds formed by consecutive pairs of the Cys residues (C31–C173 and C724–C725) (LptDC; LptD with Consecutive disulfide bods) is first generated and isomerized to LptDNC (LptD with Non-Consecutive disulfide bonds) during its assembly/maturation, which is triggered by the association of LptD with LptE (Chng et al., 2012; Narita et al., 2013).
evidence: This mechanism is supported by citations.

claim: The LptDC to LptDNC conversion should occur at a later step in the OM assembly because LptD presumably associates with LptE on the BAM complex.
source: The LptDC to LptDNC conversion should occur at a later step in the OM assembly because LptD presumably associates with LptE on the BAM complex (Chimalakonda et al., 2011; Chng et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2016; Narita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from multiple studies showing LptD-LptE association on BAM.

claim: BepA belongs to the M48 family zinc-metallopeptidases.
source: BepA (formally called YfgC), a bi-functional periplasmic protein that plays an important role in maintaining OM integrity (Narita et al., 2013), belongs to the M48 family zinc-metallopeptidases that include prokaryotic and eukaryotic proteases (such as Ste24, Oma1, and HptX) involved in membrane quality control (Rawlings et al., 2018).
evidence: This classification is supported by citation to Rawlings et al., 2018.

claim: BepA promotes the LptDC to LptDNC conversion (chaperone-like function).
source: We have previously shown that BepA is involved in the biogenesis and quality control of LptD. While BepA promotes the LptDC to LptDNC conversion (chaperone-like function) (Narita et al., 2013), it also degrades the stalled or misassembled LptDC molecules that are generated due to an lptD mutation (lptD4213) or decreased availability of or weakened interaction with LptE (protease function) (Narita et al., 2013; Soltes et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a previously established function of BepA, supported by citation.

claim: BepA degrades the stalled or misassembled LptDC molecules that are generated due to an lptD mutation (lptD4213) or decreased availability of or weakened interaction with LptE.
source: We have previously shown that BepA is involved in the biogenesis and quality control of LptD. While BepA promotes the LptDC to LptDNC conversion (chaperone-like function) (Narita et al., 2013), it also degrades the stalled or misassembled LptDC molecules that are generated due to an lptD mutation (lptD4213) or decreased availability of or weakened interaction with LptE (protease function) (Narita et al., 2013; Soltes et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a previously established function of BepA, supported by citations.

claim: BepA degrades BamA whose assembly/folding has been impaired in the absence of a periplasmic chaperone, SurA.
source: BepA also degrades BamA whose assembly/folding has been impaired in the absence of a periplasmic chaperone, SurA (Daimon et al., 2017), suggesting that BepA can also act in quality control of some other OM proteins.
evidence: This is a previously established function of BepA, supported by citation.

claim: BepA can act in quality control of some other OM proteins besides LptD.
source: BepA also degrades BamA whose assembly/folding has been impaired in the absence of a periplasmic chaperone, SurA (Daimon et al., 2017), suggesting that BepA can also act in quality control of some other OM proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that BepA degrades misfolded BamA.

claim: The BepA protein consists of an N-terminal M48 metallopeptidase domain and a C-terminal tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) domain that are associated closely to form a compact structure.
source: The BepA protein consists of an N-terminal M48 metallopeptidase domain and a C-terminal tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) domain that are associated closely to form a compact structure (Figure 1A; Bryant et al., 2020; Shahrizal et al., 2019).
evidence: This structural description is supported by citations and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The TPR domain of BepA directly interacts with LptD.
source: Our previous study suggested that the TPR domain of BepA directly interacts with LptD and with the BAM complex with its TPR domain inserted into the interior of the periplasmic part (brim) of the BAM complex (Daimon et al., 2017; Narita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is from previous work by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: The TPR domain of BepA interacts with the BAM complex with its TPR domain inserted into the interior of the periplasmic part (brim) of the BAM complex.
source: Our previous study suggested that the TPR domain of BepA directly interacts with LptD and with the BAM complex with its TPR domain inserted into the interior of the periplasmic part (brim) of the BAM complex (Daimon et al., 2017; Narita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is from previous work by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: The interactions of BepA's TPR domain with LptD and BAM are important for BepA functions.
source: A mutational study has suggested that these interactions are important for BepA functions (Daimon et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a mutational study.

claim: The His-246 residue of BepA that coordinates the zinc ion at the proteolytic active site acts as an ON/OFF switch (His switch) for the proteolytic activity of BepA.
source: Recent studies have also shown that the His-246 residue of BepA that coordinates the zinc ion at the proteolytic active site acts as an ON/OFF switch (His switch) for the proteolytic activity of BepA (Bryant et al., 2020; Daimon et al., 2020).
evidence: This mechanism is supported by recent studies cited.

claim: The unregulated expression of the proteolytic activity of BepA caused by an H246 mutation leads to the degradation of the normally assembling LptD intermediate.
source: The dual functions of BepA should be appropriately regulated because the unregulated expression of the proteolytic activity of BepA caused by an H246 mutation leads to the degradation of the normally assembling LptD intermediate (Daimon et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Daimon et al., 2020.

claim: The BepA edge-strand mutants N105P, A106P, F107P, and A108P showed significantly decreased generation of LptD degradation products.
source: We found that the expression of a few BepA mutants (N105P, A106P, F107P, and A108P) led to a significantly decreased generation of the LptD degradation products (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Some BepA edge-strand mutations compromised the degradation of BamA in a ΔsurA strain.
source: Furthermore, some of these mutations compromised the degradation of BamA in a ΔsurA strain (Daimon et al., 2017) and the self-cleavage of BepA-His10 (BepA possessing a C-terminal His10-tag) within the His10-tag (Narita et al., 2013; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Some BepA edge-strand mutations compromised the self-cleavage of BepA-His10 within the His10-tag.
source: Furthermore, some of these mutations compromised the degradation of BamA in a ΔsurA strain (Daimon et al., 2017) and the self-cleavage of BepA-His10 (BepA possessing a C-terminal His10-tag) within the His10-tag (Narita et al., 2013; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The β2-strand of BepA is important for the proteolytic activity of BepA.
source: These results strongly suggest that the β2-strand is important for the proteolytic activity of BepA.
evidence: This is inferred from the mutational analysis showing decreased proteolytic activity with edge-strand mutations.

claim: The N105pBPA, A106pBPA, F107pBPA, and A108pBPA derivatives of BepA generated UV-dependent crosslinked products that reacted with both anti-BepA and anti-LptD antibodies.
source: The N105pBPA, A106pBPA, F107pBPA, and A108pBPA derivatives of BepA generated, in a UV-dependent manner, evident crosslinked products that reacted with both anti-BepA and anti-LptD antibodies.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the photo-crosslinking data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The β2-strand of BepA directly interacts with LptD.
source: Taken together, these results imply that the β2-strand of BepA directly interacts with LptD and plays an important role in their degradation.
evidence: This is inferred from the photo-crosslinking and mutational data.

claim: The β2-strand of BepA acts as the 'edge-strand' to recognize and present a substrate to the active site.
source: The structure, intramolecular disposition, as well as involvement in substrate interaction and proteolysis of the β2-strand strongly supports the hypothesis that it indeed acts as the edge-strand to recognize and present a substrate to the active site.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural and functional data.

claim: The A106P mutant of BepA was defective in reducing LptDC accumulation.
source: We found that the A106P mutant was defective in reducing LptDC accumulation, suggesting that a mutation in the edge-strand could affect the chaperone-like function (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The acceleration of the LptDC to LptDNC conversion by the F107P and the A106P mutants was much weaker than that by the wild-type BepA.
source: The acceleration of the LptDC to LptDNC conversion by the F107P and the A106P mutants was much weaker than that by the wild-type BepA (almost the same as compared with the E137Q mutant) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the pulse-chase data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The edge-strand is important for the chaperone-like activity of BepA.
source: These results unexpectedly suggested that the edge-strand was also important for the chaperone-like activity of BepA.
evidence: This is inferred from the pulse-chase experiments showing reduced chaperone activity with edge-strand mutations.

claim: BepA Cys constructs (N105C, A106C, F107C) exhibited almost normal chaperone-like and proteolytic functions.
source: These BepA Cys constructs exhibited almost normal chaperone-like and proteolytic functions (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B and C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B and C.

claim: The secondary structure of the edge-strand is more important than the individual amino acid residues for its function.
source: This supports the idea that the secondary structure of the edge-strand is more important than the individual amino acid residues for its function, although some contribution of the side-chains of the amino acids to the functions of the edge-strand cannot be excluded.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Cys substitutions retain function while Pro substitutions do not.

claim: BepA was crosslinked mainly in the N-terminal half of the LptD β-barrel-forming domain.
source: We detected clear crosslinking with BepA mainly in the N-terminal half of the LptD β-barrel-forming domain (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the photo-crosslinking data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The residues at the BepA-cross-linkable sites in LptD were oriented both inward and outward in the mature LptD β-barrel.
source: The residues at the BepA-cross-linkable sites were oriented both inward and outward in the mature LptD β-barrel (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is shown by mapping the crosslinking sites onto the LptD structure in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The residue Gln-393 at which the strongest crosslinking was observed was oriented inward in the mature LptD β-barrel.
source: Moreover, the residue Gln-393 at which the strongest crosslinking was observed was oriented inward.
evidence: This is observed from the crosslinking data and structural mapping.

claim: LptD while interacting with BepA would not assume a higher-order structure like closed β-barrel.
source: These results suggest that LptD while interacting with BepA would not assume a higher-order structure like closed β-barrel (see Discussion).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both inward and outward-facing residues are crosslinked with BepA.

claim: The LptD(pBPA) derivatives that showed crosslinking with BepA were functional.
source: We selected a few LptD(pBPA) derivatives that had been crosslinked with BepA as representatives and examined their functionality. They supported the growth of LptD-depleted cells when expressed from a plasmid, indicating that they were functional (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the complementation assay shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The crosslinking results likely reflect a functional interaction of LptD with BepA in the normal assembly pathway.
source: The above-mentioned crosslinking results thus likely reflect a functional interaction of LptD with BepA in the normal assembly pathway.
evidence: This is inferred from the functionality of the crosslinked LptD derivatives.

claim: The F107P mutation significantly decreased the efficiency of the crosslinking of BepA(N105pBPA) and BepA(A106pBPA) with LptD.
source: The F107P mutation significantly decreased the efficiency of the crosslinking of BepA(N105pBPA) and BepA(A106pBPA) with LptD (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The A106P mutation exhibited a similar effect on the crosslinking of BepA(N105pBPA) with LptD.
source: Additionally, the A106P mutation exhibited a similar effect on the crosslinking of BepA(N105pBPA) with LptD.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The F107P and A106P mutations in the BepA edge-strand markedly decreased the amount of crosslinked products for LptD(Y331pBPA).
source: We found that these mutations altered LptD–BepA crosslinking in a site-specific manner. Further, the amount of crosslinked products markedly decreased for LptD(Y331pBPA), but not for other mutants (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The region around Tyr-331 in the β7 strand of the LptD β-barrel domain is crosslinked with the edge-strand of BepA.
source: These results strongly suggest that the region around Tyr-331 in the β7 strand of the LptD β-barrel domain (Figure 2D) is crosslinked with the edge-strand of BepA.
evidence: This is inferred from the site-specific effects of edge-strand mutations on crosslinking.

claim: The combination of BepA(N105C) and LptD(Y331C) showed the most intense disulfide crosslinked band.
source: We observed that certain combinations of BepA and LptD derivatives showed a high-molecular-mass band in electrophoresis results. Among them, the combination of BepA(N105C) and LptD(Y331C) showed the most intense band that exhibited reaction with the anti-BepA antibody (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, no ME).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The high-molecular-mass bands observed in disulfide crosslinking were disulfide-crosslinked products.
source: These high-molecular-mass bands were not observed with the wild-type LptD (no additional Cys) and disappeared upon treatment with ME, suggesting that they were disulfide-crosslinked products (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, + ME).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ME-sensitivity of the bands shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The edge-strand of BepA can directly bind to several regions in the N-terminal half of the LptD β-barrel-forming domain, which includes the β7 strand containing Tyr-331.
source: These results are consistent with the photo-crosslinking experiments (Figure 3A) and indicate that the edge-strand of BepA can directly bind to several regions in the N-terminal half of the LptD β-barrel-forming domain, which includes the β7 strand containing Tyr-331.
evidence: This is inferred from both photo-crosslinking and disulfide crosslinking data.

claim: LptD4213 interacts with the seam region formed by the N- and C-terminal β-strands (β1 and β16, respectively) in the BamA barrel domain.
source: It has been recently shown that LptD4213, a mutant form of LptD that has a short (23 amino acids) deletion in an extracellular loop (eL4) and is stalled on the BAM complex mimicking a late assembly complex (Lee et al., 2016), interacts with the seam region formed by the N- and C-terminal β-strands (β1 and β16, respectively) in the BamA barrel domain and forms a hetero-complex, in which the C-terminal β-signal of the LptD4213 was associated with the β1 strand of the BamA seam (Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2016 and 2019.

claim: The C-terminal β-signal of LptD4213 was associated with the β1 strand of the BamA seam.
source: It has been recently shown that LptD4213, a mutant form of LptD that has a short (23 amino acids) deletion in an extracellular loop (eL4) and is stalled on the BAM complex mimicking a late assembly complex (Lee et al., 2016), interacts with the seam region formed by the N- and C-terminal β-strands (β1 and β16, respectively) in the BamA barrel domain and forms a hetero-complex, in which the C-terminal β-signal of the LptD4213 was associated with the β1 strand of the BamA seam (Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2019.

claim: The interaction of the β-signal with the BamA β1 strand generally facilitates the folding of the β-barrel domain of a substrate OMP.
source: It has been suggested that the interaction of the β-signal with the BamA β1 strand generally facilitates the folding of the β-barrel domain of a substrate OMP (see Figure 4D and 5B; Tomasek and Kahne, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tomasek and Kahne, 2021.

claim: LptD(Y331pBPA) was crosslinked with BepA.
source: The single pBPA derivatives indeed generated crosslinked products with the expected factors as: LptD(Y331pBPA) with BepA, LptD(D749pBPA) with BamA, and LptD(Y726pBPA) with BamD (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: LptD(D749pBPA) was crosslinked with BamA.
source: The single pBPA derivatives indeed generated crosslinked products with the expected factors as: LptD(Y331pBPA) with BepA, LptD(D749pBPA) with BamA, and LptD(Y726pBPA) with BamD (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: LptD(Y726pBPA) was crosslinked with BamD.
source: The single pBPA derivatives indeed generated crosslinked products with the expected factors as: LptD(Y331pBPA) with BepA, LptD(D749pBPA) with BamA, and LptD(Y726pBPA) with BamD (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: The double pBPA derivatives LptD(Y331/D749pBPA) and LptD(Y331/Y726pBPA) generated new crosslinked products with higher molecular sizes representing BepA–LptD–BamA and BepA–LptD–BamD crosslinked products.
source: With the double pBPA derivatives LptD(Y331/D749pBPA) and LptD(Y331/Y726pBPA), new crosslinked products with higher molecular sizes were observed in addition to the ones observed with single pBPA mutants (Figure 4A and B). These results showed that the higher molecular-sized products represented BepA–LptD(Y331/D749pBPA)–BamA and BepA–LptD(Y331/Y726pBPA)–BamD crosslinked products and that BepA interacts with an assembly intermediate of LptD on the BAM complex.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: BepA interacts with an assembly intermediate of LptD on the BAM complex.
source: With the double pBPA derivatives LptD(Y331/D749pBPA) and LptD(Y331/Y726pBPA), new crosslinked products with higher molecular sizes were observed in addition to the ones observed with single pBPA mutants (Figure 4A and B). These results showed that the higher molecular-sized products represented BepA–LptD(Y331/D749pBPA)–BamA and BepA–LptD(Y331/Y726pBPA)–BamD crosslinked products and that BepA interacts with an assembly intermediate of LptD on the BAM complex.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ternary crosslinking products shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: A cysteine placed near the N-terminal β-strand of the BamA β-barrel (S439C) was crosslinked with a cysteine introduced near the β-signal of LptD (E733C) via BMB treatment.
source: It has been previously shown (Lee et al., 2019) that a cysteine placed near the N-terminal β-strand of the BamA β-barrel (S439C) was crosslinked with a cysteine introduced near the β-signal of LptD (E733C) via BMB treatment (Figure 4D; Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2019 and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: When cells expressing LptD(Y331pBPA/E733C) in a bamA(S439C) strain were first treated with BMB and then UV-irradiated, a higher mass product that reacted with both anti-BepA and anti-BamA antibodies was generated.
source: When cells were first treated with BMB and then UV-irradiated, a higher mass product that reacted with both anti-BepA and anti-BamA antibodies was generated. The generation of this product depended on both BMB-treatment and UV-irradiation (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: BepA could interact with an LptD assembly intermediate associating with the seam site of BamA on the BAM complex.
source: These results are fully consistent with the above photo-crosslinking results and further demonstrated that BepA could interact with an LptD assembly intermediate associating with the seam site of BamA on the BAM complex.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the combined BMB and photo-crosslinking experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Zinc-metallopeptidases usually possess a β-strand, called edge-strand, located close to their proteolytic active sites.
source: Zinc-metallopeptidases usually possess a β-strand, called edge-strand, located close to their proteolytic active sites (Akiyama et al., 2015; López-Pelegrín et al., 2013; Stöcker and Bode, 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge about metallopeptidases, supported by citations.

claim: The edge-strand plays a critical role in substrate proteolysis by directly interacting with a substrate polypeptide by the strand addition mechanism and converts it into an extended conformation for its presentation to the active site and proteolysis.
source: While the edge-strand is known to play a critical role in substrate proteolysis by directly interacting with a substrate polypeptide by the strand addition mechanism and converts it into an extended conformation for its presentation to the active site and proteolysis, it has not been well characterized in M48 proteases.
evidence: This is established knowledge about edge-strand function, though not well characterized in M48 proteases.

claim: BepA has a β-strand (β2) that is conserved among the M48-peptidases and is located adjacent to the active site.
source: The solved structures of Escherichia coli BepA (Bryant et al., 2020; Shahrizal et al., 2019) show that it has a β-strand (β2) that is conserved among the M48-peptidases and is located adjacent to the active site (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1), suggesting that this strand presumably acts as an edge-strand.
evidence: This is shown in the BepA structures cited and in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: When LptD is overproduced from a multi-copy plasmid, it mainly accumulates in the form of LptDC possibly due to the limited availability of its partner protein, LptE.
source: When LptD is overproduced from a multi-copy plasmid, it mainly accumulates in the form of LptDC possibly due to the limited availability of its partner protein, LptE (Daimon et al., 2020; Daimon et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Overproduced LptDC probably represents a 'normal' assembly intermediate as it is associated with the BAM complex.
source: This species probably represents a 'normal' assembly intermediate as it is associated with the BAM complex (see below) and can be converted to the mature form (LptDNC) when LptE is co-expressed (Miyazaki et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation and by data shown later in the manuscript.

claim: Overproduced LptDC can be converted to the mature form (LptDNC) when LptE is co-expressed.
source: This species probably represents a 'normal' assembly intermediate as it is associated with the BAM complex (see below) and can be converted to the mature form (LptDNC) when LptE is co-expressed (Miyazaki et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Miyazaki et al., 2018.

claim: Overproduced LptD was degraded by co-expressed wild-type BepA to generate discrete degradation products.
source: As reported previously (Daimon et al., 2020; Daimon et al., 2017), overproduced LptD was degraded by co-expressed wild-type BepA to generate discrete degradation products (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B and supported by citations.

claim: The BepA-crosslinked positions in LptD were located in the N-terminal half of the β-barrel-forming domain.
source: We detected clear crosslinking with BepA mainly in the N-terminal half of the LptD β-barrel-forming domain (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A and summarized in Figure 2C.

claim: The BepA-interacting region of the LptD intermediate is largely unstructured.
source: Collectively, these results support the hypothesis that the BepA-interacting region of the LptD intermediate is largely unstructured.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both inward and outward-facing residues in the mature barrel are crosslinked with BepA.

claim: The proper interaction of LptD with the edge-strand of BepA is important for the promotion of its assembly as well as degradation by BepA.
source: Further, our results suggest that the proper interaction of LptD with the edge-strand of BepA is important for the promotion of its assembly as well as degradation by BepA (Figure 1 and Figure 5A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the mutational and functional analyses shown in Figure 1.

claim: The His-switch-mediated repression of the protease activity enables the interaction of LptD intermediates at the protease active site of BepA without degradation.
source: This His-switch-mediated repression of the protease activity would enable the interaction of LptD intermediates at the protease active site of BepA without degradation.
evidence: This is inferred from the His-switch mechanism and the observation that edge-strand interaction is required for both functions.

claim: The derepressed BepA(H246A) mutant degrades an LptD intermediate on the normal assembly pathway, instead of promoting its biogenesis.
source: Indeed, the derepressed BepA(H246A) mutant degrades an LptD intermediate on the normal assembly pathway, instead of promoting its biogenesis (Daimon et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Daimon et al., 2020.

claim: The transient interaction of normally assembling LptD with the 'protease activity-repressed' state of BepA would provide sufficient time for the progression of the maturation processes of LptD.
source: The transient interaction of normally assembling LptD with the 'protease activity-repressed' state of BepA would provide sufficient time for the progression of the maturation processes of LptD (including association with LptE), resulting in the final release of mature LptD from BamA.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the data and previous findings.

claim: During the prolonged stay of stalled or misassembled LptD molecules, BepA undergoes a further structural change to remove His-246 from the active site zinc, leading to the degradation of the molecules that cannot be subjected to maturation successfully.
source: In contrast, during the prolonged stay of stalled or misassembled LptD molecules, BepA undergoes a further structural change including the movement of the α9-loop, stochastically or induced by a specific signal(s) that was transmitted from the BAM complex and/or LptD through their interaction with BepA, to remove His-246 from the active site zinc, leading to the degradation of the molecules that cannot be subjected to maturation successfully.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the data.

claim: The conversion of LptDC to LptDNC started immediately after the synthesis of LptD and proceeded rather constantly.
source: Our previous results of pulse-chase experiments showed that, although the conversion of LptDC to LptDNC was relatively slow, it started immediately after the synthesis of LptD and proceeded rather constantly (Narita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Degradation of stalled LptD in an LptE-depleted strain apparently occurred in a biphasic manner with a lag period.
source: In contrast, degradation of stalled LptD in an LptE-depleted strain apparently occurred in a biphasic manner; little degradation of stalled LptD was observed for several minutes after synthesis (Narita et al., 2013), indicating the presence of a lag period for degradation of stalled LptD to occur.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: BepA expression can result in the degradation of LptD4213 that probably mimics a late-state assembly intermediate of LptD.
source: Notably, it has been reported that BepA expression can result in the degradation of a mutant form of LptD (LptD4213) that probably mimics a late-state assembly intermediate of LptD (Lee et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2016) that possesses a substantial degree of a higher order (β-barrel-like) structure and interacts with the Bam components (BamA and BamD), and LptE.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2016 and 2019.

claim: BepA possibly facilitates the association of LptD with LptE on the BAM complex.
source: BepA possibly facilitates the association of LptD with LptE on the BAM complex as the phenotypes caused by the disruption of BepA, including drug sensitivity and retarded disulfide rearrangement in LptD, can be suppressed by the overproduction of LptE (Narita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the suppression of ΔbepA phenotypes by LptE overproduction, supported by citation.

claim: Two species of LptDC exist: one not associated with LptE observed only in an extremely early phase of membrane assembly, and the other associated with LptE formed at a later phase.
source: We have previously detected two species of LptDC; one is not associated with LptE and observed only in an extremely early phase of its membrane assembly, and the other is associated with LptE and formed at a later phase (Miyazaki et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The LptDC molecule that was simultaneously crosslinked with BepA and BamA was not associated with LptE.
source: It is likely that the LptDC molecule that was simultaneously crosslinked with BepA and BamA was not associated with LptE, as it was accumulated in the LptE-limiting condition; therefore, it would represent the former species of LptDC mentioned above.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental conditions (LptE-limiting) used for the crosslinking experiments.

claim: The LptD intermediate crosslinked with BepA and BamA may possess a partially folded structure in which the BamA-associating C-terminal region of the barrel domain has a certain degree of a higher order (β-sheet) structure, but the BepA-associating N-terminal region is largely unstructured.
source: We assume that this LptD intermediate may possess a partially folded structure in which the BamA-associating C-terminal region of the barrel domain has a certain degree of a higher order (β-sheet) structure, but the BepA-associating N-terminal region is largely unstructured.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the crosslinking data.

claim: Tyr-331 of LptD that contacts with the edge-strand of BepA is located at the end of the LptE-surrounding region of the LptD β-barrel in the mature LptD/E complex.
source: Interestingly, Tyr-331 of LptD that contacts with the edge-strand of BepA is located at the end of the LptE-surrounding region of the LptD β-barrel in the mature LptD/E complex (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The interaction with the edge-strand of BepA may pin the partially folded structure of LptD transiently and facilitate the association between LptD and LptE.
source: The interaction with the edge-strand of BepA may pin the partially folded structure of LptD transiently and facilitate the association between LptD and LptE.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the crosslinking data and structural considerations.

claim: After synthesis in the cytoplasm, LptD is translocated to the periplasm through the SecYEG translocon, during or just after which the Cys residues are oxidized by DsbA to form LptDC.
source: (i) After synthesis in the cytoplasm, LptD is translocated to the periplasm through the SecYEG translocon, during or just after which the Cys residues are oxidized by DsbA to form LptDC (Chng et al., 2012; Narita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model, supported by citations.

claim: LptD is targeted to the BAM complex with the aid of periplasmic chaperones including SurA.
source: It is then targeted to the BAM complex with the aid of periplasmic chaperones including SurA (Schwalm et al., 2013; Vertommen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model, supported by citations.

claim: The C-terminal β-signal region of LptD is inserted into the BAM complex possibly through the periplasmic ring-like structure formed by the BamA POTRA domains and the lipoprotein subunits of the BAM complex, and it establishes interaction with BamD and BamA.
source: (ii) The C-terminal β-signal region of LptD is inserted into the BAM complex possibly through the periplasmic ring-like structure formed by the BamA POTRA domains and the lipoprotein subunits of the BAM complex, and it establishes interaction with BamD and BamA (Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model, supported by citation.

claim: BepA with its protease activity repressed by His-246 residue interacts with the largely unstructured N-terminal half of the LptD β-barrel-forming domain whose C-terminal β-signal region is associated with the seam region of BamA.
source: (iii) Although details of the exact juncture at which interaction occurs are unknown, BepA with its protease activity repressed by His-246 residue interacts with the largely unstructured N-terminal half of the LptD β-barrel-forming domain whose C-terminal β-signal region is associated with the seam region of BamA.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the crosslinking data.

claim: BepA stabilizes the partially unfolded assembly intermediate of LptD on the BAM complex to help the association of LptE with LptD.
source: This stabilizes the partially unfolded assembly intermediate of LptD on the BAM complex to help the association of LptE with LptD.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model.

claim: The folding (β-sheet formation) of the unstructured N-terminal region of the LptD β-barrel domain occurs to form a premature form of LptD with a substantially folded β-barrel domain and LptE within it.
source: (iv) Then, the folding (β-sheet formation) of the unstructured N-terminal region of the LptD β-barrel domain occurs to form a premature form of LptD with a substantially folded β-barrel domain and LptE within it, like LptD4213 (Lee et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model, supported by citations.

claim: The β-barrel domain of LptD is finally released from BamA and closed to form the mature LptD/E complex.
source: (v) The β-barrel domain of LptD β-barrel is finally released from BamA and closed to form the mature LptD/E complex.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model.

claim: The isomerization of two disulfide bonds in LptD (LptDC to LptDNC) should occur at a later step after the association of LptD and LptE.
source: The isomerization of two disulfide bonds in LptD (LptDC to LptDNC) should occur at a later step after the association of LptD and LptE (Lee et al., 2016; Miyazaki et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: The LptD intermediates that are stalled at certain steps in the assembly process as a result of misfolding are eliminated by the action of several peptidases including DegP (in the periplasm) and BepA/YcaL (on the BAM complex).
source: The LptD intermediates that are stalled at certain steps in the above-mentioned processes as a result of misfolding are eliminated by the action of several peptidases including DegP (in the periplasm) and BepA /YcaL (on the BAM complex) (Soltes et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Soltes et al., 2017.

claim: A ternary complex formation among an assembly intermediate of an OM protein (EspP, an autotransporter), a periplasmic chaperone (SurA/Skp), and the BAM complex has been suggested from biochemical studies including crosslinking.
source: A ternary complex formation among an assembly intermediate of an OM protein (EspP, an autotransporter), a periplasmic chaperone (SurA/Skp), and the BAM complex has been suggested form biochemical studies including crosslinking, although the ternary complex was not directly detected (Ieva et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ieva et al., 2011.

claim: The ternary complex formation for LptD, BepA, and the BAM complex was experimentally demonstrated.
source: We here experimentally demonstrated the ternary complex formation for LptD, BepA, and the BAM complex.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the crosslinking experiments shown in Figure 4.
